config.brief:
Build a mobile app called **MedGuard AI** — an offline-first, on-device AI skin & wound triage assistant for ASHA workers and rural health center staff in India, with an agentic clinical-guidance layer that activates when internet connectivity is available.

CONTEXT: Rural health workers lack dermatologist/wound-care access and reliable connectivity. Existing tools are either cloud-dependent (useless offline) or single-model image classifiers with no clinical context, no safety validation, and no evidence-grounded guidance. This app must work fully offline for image capture, AI classification, and risk triage, and layer in RAG-based clinical-guideline retrieval plus a multi-agent validation chain (Triage → Protocol → Safety → Referral, orchestrated by a Supervisor) only when online — never blocking the core workflow on connectivity.

TECH ASSUMPTIONS: Android-first, React Native or Flutter shell, on-device TensorFlow Lite model for image classification + risk tiering, local SQLite/Room database for offline-first storage, background sync service, encrypted local storage for images and patient data, cloud backend with a RAG pipeline over WHO/ICMR clinical guidelines for online-mode recommendations.

Build the following screens, each with the exact features and logic described:

**1. Splash Screen** — Load the TFLite model into memory on launch so there's no delay later during capture. Check the local DB for unsynced pending cases and set a badge count. Check connectivity once (non-blocking) and set a global isOnline flag used app-wide. Route to Login if no active session, else to Home Dashboard.

**2. Login / Worker Onboarding** — Fields: worker ID/phone, PIN or OTP (OTP only if online, PIN as offline fallback), "Register new worker" link, language selector. Auth must work fully offline after first-time setup: store a local PIN hash, validate against it with no network call needed for returning logins. First-time registration captures name, ID, PHC/health-center affiliation, phone; stores locally and syncs to cloud once online. Persist language choice across sessions. Store session token securely (Android Keystore / EncryptedSharedPreferences).

**3. Home Dashboard** — Primary large CTA "New Case." Connectivity indicator chip (Online/Offline). Pending-sync count badge. Recent cases list (last 5) with color-coded risk chips (green/amber/red). Quick stats: cases today, high-risk cases pending referral. Nav to Patient History, Sync Center, Settings. Logic: pull recent cases from local DB sorted by timestamp descending; use event-driven connectivity detection (OS network callback), not constant polling; if the device regains connectivity while unsynced high-risk cases exist, auto-trigger background sync and show a toast notification.

**4. New Case → Patient Metadata Screen** — Form fields: patient name/ID or anonymized token, age, sex, duration of illness/wound in days, diabetes status (yes/no/unknown), fever (yes/no + temp if known), pain level (0–10 slider), known allergies/medical history (free text or checklist), optional condition-category hint (skin lesion / wound / rash / other). Logic: only age and condition category are required, all else optional so workers aren't blocked when in a rush — but flag downstream to the Triage Agent as "low-confidence, metadata incomplete" if too sparse. Autosave every field change to a local draft case record to survive app kill or battery loss mid-entry. On submit, generate a local UUID case_id and pass structured metadata forward to the vision pipeline.

**5. Image Capture Screen** — Camera viewfinder with on-screen framing guide overlay and a prompt like "fill frame, avoid shadow." Flash toggle, retake button, gallery-import fallback. Real-time image-quality feedback (blur/glare/lighting warning). Option to capture up to 3 angles per case. Logic: run an on-device quality check immediately after capture — blur detection via Laplacian variance, brightness histogram check — and reject unusable photos with specific retake guidance (e.g., "Too dark — move to better light") before they reach the classifier. Apply CLAHE-style contrast normalization automatically before inference for lighting consistency. Save accepted images to encrypted local storage; never auto-upload. Queue multiple images from one case for a single inference pass, letting the Triage Agent use the best/majority verdict.

**6. On-Device AI Analysis (Processing Screen)** — Animated progress with staged labels: "Preprocessing image…", "Running classification…", "Cross-checking with patient details…", plus an estimated time remaining. Logic: run the TFLite model for multiclass classification (e.g., melanoma-suspect, diabetic foot ulcer, eczema, psoriasis, fungal infection, normal/benign, other) plus a Low/Moderate/High risk-tier head. Generate an explainability heatmap (Grad-CAM or similar) from the same forward pass and store it with the prediction. Package model output plus patient metadata into a structured object and hand off to the on-device, rule-based Triage Agent — no LLM or network call required at this stage. If confidence is below threshold, still proceed to the Result screen but mark the case "Uncertain — recommend in-person exam" rather than failing.

**7. Triage Result Screen** — Large color-coded risk banner (green=Low, amber=Moderate, red=High/Urgent). Predicted condition label with confidence percentage. Original photo with a toggleable explainability heatmap overlay. A plain-language explanation line describing what visual patterns drove the flag. An expandable "Why this risk level?" section showing which metadata factors influenced the score (e.g., "Fever + wound duration >7 days increased urgency"). Buttons: View Care Guidance, View Agent Validation, Save & Continue. Logic: the risk banner color is driven by the Triage Agent's fused decision (image confidence plus metadata rules), not the raw model output alone — e.g. moderate image confidence plus fever plus diabetes can escalate to High even if the vision model alone said Moderate. Render the explainability overlay from the stored heatmap tensor without recomputation. This entire screen must work fully offline.

**8. Agent Validation Detail Screen** — Vertical checklist/timeline showing each agent's verdict: Triage Agent (risk classification + confidence), Protocol Agent (whether findings align with known clinical patterns — rule-based offline, RAG-refined online), Safety Agent (flags contradictions or danger signs, can force mandatory human review), Referral Agent (final recommendation: self-care / clinic visit / urgent referral). Logic: Supervisor orchestrates Triage → Protocol and Safety in parallel → Referral synthesizes the final call. The Safety Agent has veto power — it can override a "Low risk" verdict to "Recommend clinical review" if a contradiction rule fires (e.g., diabetic + foot wound + long duration must never resolve as pure self-care regardless of image confidence). Offline, all agents run as deterministic rule engines plus the local model; online, the Protocol Agent additionally queries the RAG pipeline against WHO/ICMR guideline embeddings for a richer, citation-backed justification, appended to this screen retroactively once sync completes ("Updated guidance available").

**9. Clinical Guideline / Care Recommendation Screen** — Numbered, plain-language immediate-care steps. Tappable source citation chip (e.g., "WHO Wound Care Guideline, Sec. 4.2") showing more context. A "This is guidance, not a diagnosis" disclaimer banner. Optional medication-availability note if integrated with a local facility inventory feed. Logic: if online, query the RAG pipeline with predicted condition, risk tier, and relevant metadata, retrieve top-k guideline chunks, and generate a concise recommendation grounded in the retrieved text. If offline, fall back to a pre-packaged static guideline snippet for that condition/risk combination bundled with the app, so the worker is never left with nothing. Timestamp and version every recommendation so audits can trace which guideline version informed a case.

**10. Referral & Facility Locator Screen** — Map view with offline-cached tiles for the worker's registered region, pins for nearest PHC/CHC/hospital. List-view fallback with facility name, distance, type, phone number. "Generate Referral Note" button producing a printable/shareable summary (condition, risk level, photo, metadata). Call-facility button that works over phone connectivity independent of data. Logic: pre-load the facility database locally per district during setup/sync so the locator works offline, refreshing opportunistically when online. Auto-populate the referral note from the case record, letting the worker add free-text notes before sharing via SMS, print, or Bluetooth printer. For High-risk cases, auto-surface this screen immediately after the Result screen rather than requiring manual navigation.

**11. Case Summary / Save Screen** — Full recap of metadata, image, risk level, recommendation, and referral status, with Edit/Save/Discard options and a per-case sync-status indicator. Logic: save the finalized case to the local DB marked "pending sync" if offline; never transmit anything until connectivity is available and the worker hasn't opted out of sync for that case (privacy control).

**12. Patient History Screen** — Searchable/filterable list of past cases (by risk level, date range, condition, sync status), tapping into a read-only Case Detail view. Logic: query is local-first against the on-device DB with no network dependency; support re-opening a past case to log an outcome (e.g., "patient referred and treated") that feeds back into future model/agent evaluation.

**13. Sync Center** — List of pending items (cases, worker registrations, facility DB updates) with a manual "Sync Now" button, per-item status (queued/uploading/failed/done), and a data-usage estimate. Logic: background sync triggers automatically on Wi-Fi or when mobile data is available and the user has allowed it, respecting data-cost sensitivity in rural contexts. Failed uploads retry with exponential backoff; duplicate-case conflicts resolve via UUID-based idempotency. Encrypt all patient images/data at rest and in transit.

**14. Settings / Profile Screen** — Worker profile edit, language selection, data-sync preference (Wi-Fi only vs. any network), model version info, storage usage, an offline map/guideline bundle download manager, and logout. Logic: deliver model and guideline-bundle updates as downloadable packages the worker fetches manually when connectivity is good, rather than forcing background updates that consume limited data.

CROSS-CUTTING REQUIREMENTS TO ENFORCE THROUGHOUT:
- Privacy-by-design: all inference runs on-device; raw images never leave the phone unless the worker explicitly syncs a case, and even then transmission is encrypted.
- Graceful degradation ladder for guidance: full RAG-grounded advice (online) → cached static guideline bundle (offline) → generic safety-first fallback message (worst case) — the app must never show a blank or unhelpful screen for a risk result.
- The Safety Agent's mandatory-review flag can never be suppressed by any other agent's verdict; enforce this at the orchestration layer, not just in the UI.
- Explainability heatmaps and the full agent reasoning chain are persisted with each case record, not shown only once, to support later clinical audit and build worker trust over time.
config.constraints:
This is a decision-support tool, not a diagnostic device. Never phrase any UI copy, notification, or generated text as a diagnosis, prescription, or medical certainty. Always frame output as "risk flag," "suggested next step," or "recommendation for a health worker to consider" — never "the patient has X."
Offline is the default state, not the fallback state. Design every screen assuming no connectivity first, then layer online enhancements on top. Nothing on the core capture-to-referral path may block, spin indefinitely, or silently fail when the network is unavailable.
No cloud call may be synchronous with the triage workflow. RAG/guideline retrieval, agent LLM refinement, and cloud sync must all be background/async operations that enhance an already-complete offline result — never a blocking dependency for producing a risk level.
The Safety Agent's authority is architectural, not cosmetic. Implement its override as a hard rule in the orchestration/business logic layer (e.g., a non-bypassable check before the Referral Agent finalizes output), not just a UI warning badge that a user could ignore or a screen that could be skipped.
Never fabricate clinical content. All care-guidance text must trace to either (a) a retrieved WHO/ICMR guideline chunk with a citation, or (b) a pre-approved static offline snippet reviewed by a clinical advisor — never freely generated by a model with no grounding. If neither source is available, show the generic safety-first fallback ("recommend in-person evaluation") rather than inventing advice.
Data minimization and consent. Only collect patient metadata that directly feeds the triage/referral logic; do not add speculative fields "for later." Make clear in the UI (at Patient Metadata screen) that data stays on-device until the worker explicitly syncs, and let the worker opt out of syncing a specific sensitive case.
Design for low digital literacy and low-end hardware. Favor large tap targets, minimal text entry, icon+color coding over dense text, and short load/inference times on budget Android devices (assume 2–3GB RAM, mid-range or older chipsets) — the on-device model must stay lightweight (target well under 20MB, similar to the FixCaps/LesionNet benchmarks in the literature).
Language and literacy support are first-class, not an afterthought. All patient-facing and worker-facing strings must be structured for easy localization from the start (no hardcoded English strings baked into logic), and critical risk/referral messaging should support voice/audio playback for low-literacy users where feasible.
Scope discipline for MVP. Build the 14 screens and flow as specified; do not add speculative features (e.g., video consults, e-pharmacy ordering, wearable integration) unless explicitly requested — the differentiators to prioritize are: on-device vision, multi-agent safety validation, RAG-grounded guidance, and offline-first operation.
Auditability by design. Every case record must retain enough information (model version, guideline version, agent verdicts, heatmap, metadata snapshot) to reconstruct exactly why a recommendation was made, months later, for clinical review or research purposes.
Fail safe, not fail silent. Any component failure (model load error, corrupted image, sync failure, low storage) must degrade to a clearly communicated safe state ("Unable to analyze — please refer patient for manual evaluation") rather than a crash, blank screen, or incorrect low-risk default.
